title: Medieval History: Early Medieval History (Rajputs, Arab invasion) (Test)

questions.q_en: Which of the following statements best explains the significance of Kannauj during the Tripartite Struggle?
options_en: It was the religious capital of Northern India.
Kannauj was a commercially strategic city due to its location on the Ganga trade route.
Kannauj was primarily a cultural hub under the Gupta Empire.
Kannauj was a fortified city that remained unconquered during this period.
questions.solution_en:
• Kannauj was commercially strategic due to its position on the Ganga trade route, which made it an essential center for controlling trade between North and Eastern India.

• This economic importance was the main reason for the struggle between the Gurjara-Pratiharas, Palas, and Rashtrakutas.

Further Insight:

• Tripartite Struggle for Kannauj Supremacy (750-1000 CE)

○ Major Empires: Gurjara-Pratihara (Western India), Palas (Eastern India), Rashtrakutas (Deccan).

○ Cause: Control over Kannauj, a commercially strategic location on the Ganga trade route and previously the capital of Harshavardhan.
questions.solution_hi:
• कन्नौज गंगा व्यापार मार्ग पर अपनी स्थिति के कारण वाणिज्यिक रूप से रणनीतिक था, जिसने इसे उत्तर व पूर्वी भारत के बीच व्यापार नियंत्रित करने हेतु एक आवश्यक केंद्र बनाया।

• यह आर्थिक महत्व गुर्जर-प्रतिहार, पाल व राष्ट्रकूट के बीच संघर्ष का मुख्य कारण था।

questions.q_en: Which of the following rulers is credited with the reconstruction of the Somnath temple after Arab raids?
questions.solution_en:
• Nagabhata II is credited with rebuilding the Somnath temple after it was damaged by Arab invasions.

• Nagabhata I is noted for repelling early Arab invasions but didn't rebuild the temple.

• Mihir Bhoja is known for consolidating the empire and adopting the title 'Adivaraha'.

• Vatsaraja initiated the Tripartite Struggle but wasn't involved with the Somnath temple.

Further Insight:

• Important Rulers of Gurjara-Pratihara Dynasty (730-1036)

○ Nagabhatta I (730-760):

■ Famed for containing Arab invasions.

■ Defeated by Rashtrakuta king Dhruva.

○ Vatsaraja (780-800):

■ Made Kannauj his capital, initiating the "Tripartite Struggle."

■ Defeated Pala ruler Dharmapala and Rashtrakuta king Dantidurga.

○ Nagabhata II (805-833):

■ Conquered Kannauj and rebuilt Somnath temple after Arab raids.

○ Bhoja I / Mihir Bhoja (836-885):

■ Greatest Pratihara ruler, adopted the title 'Adivaraha.'
questions.solution_hi:
• नागभट्ट द्वितीय को अरब आक्रमणों से क्षतिग्रस्त होने के बाद सोमनाथ मंदिर के पुनर्निर्माण का श्रेय जाता है।

• नागभट्ट प्रथम प्रारंभिक अरब आक्रमणों को रोकने के लिए जाने जाते हैं परंतु उन्होंने मंदिर का पुनर्निर्माण नहीं किया।

• मिहिर भोज साम्राज्य को सुदृढ़ करने व 'आदिवराह' उपाधि अपनाने के लिए जाने जाते हैं।

questions.q_en: Which of the following Pala rulers is famous for founding Vikramshila University?
questions.solution_en:
• Dharampala is credited with founding Vikramshila University, which became a major center for Buddhist learning, complementing Nalanda.

• Gopala founded the Pala dynasty .

• Devapala expanded the Pala Empire but is not connected to Vikramshila.

Further Insight:

• Important ruler of the Palas of Bengal (750-1150)

○ Gopala (750 CE):

■ Founder of Pala Dynasty

■ Founded Odantapuri monastery, the second-largest after Nalanda.

○ Dharampala (770-810):

■ Founded Vikramshila University and revived Nalanda University.

○ Devapala (810-850):

■ Expanded empire, known for victories over Hunas, Gurjaras, and Dravidas.
questions.solution_hi:
• धर्मपाल को विक्रमशिला विश्वविद्यालय की स्थापना का श्रेय जाता है, जो नालंदा के साथ बौद्ध शिक्षा का एक प्रमुख केंद्र बना।

• गोपाल ने पाल वंश की स्थापना की।

• देवपाल ने पाल साम्राज्य का विस्तार किया परंतु विक्रमशिला से जुड़े नहीं हैं।

questions.q_en: Which Rashtrakuta king is associated with the construction of the Kailasanath Temple at Ellora?
questions.solution_en:
• Krishna I, who succeeded Dantidurga, is renowned for commissioning the Kailasanath Temple, an architectural marvel carved from a single rock.

• Dantidurga is known for founding the Rashtrakuta kingdom.

Further Insight:

• Important Rulers of Rashtrakutas of Deccan (752-973)

○ Dantidurga (753-756):

■ Founded Rashtrakuta kingdom.

○ Krishna I (756-774):

■ Defeated Pallavas and built the famous Kailasanath (Shiva) temple at Ellora.

○ Amoghavarsha I (814-878):

■ Compared to Ashoka, built a new capital at Manyakheta. Authored Kavirajamarga (Kannada) and Prashnottara Ratnamalika (Sanskrit).
questions.solution_hi:
• दंतिदुर्ग के उत्तराधिकारी कृष्ण प्रथम, एक ही चट्टान से तराशे गए वास्तुकला के चमत्कार, कैलासनाथ मंदिर का निर्माण करवाने के लिए प्रसिद्ध हैं।

• दंतिदुर्ग राष्ट्रकूट राज्य की स्थापना के लिए जाने जाते हैं।

• दक्कन के राष्ट्रकूटों (752-973) के महत्वपूर्ण शासक।

questions.q_en: Which of the following titles was assumed by Rajendra I after his conquest of the Ganges valley?
questions.solution_en:
• After his successful northern campaign up to the Ganges valley, Rajendra I assumed the title "Gangaikondachola" (the Chola who conquered the Ganga).

Further Insight:

• Important ruler of the Chola dynasty (985-1044 CE)

• Founding: By Vijayalaya, a feudatory of Pallavas. The Imperial Cholas were based in Tanjore.

• Key Rulers

○ Rajaraja I (985-1014 AD):

■ Expanded Chola empire, conquered Maldives, and built the Rajarajeshwara or Brihadeshwara temple at Thanjavur.

○ Rajendra I (1014-1044 AD):

■ Conquered Sri Lanka, assumed the title "Gangaikondachola," and built a new capital city, Gangaikondacholapuram.

○ Chola Architecture: Dravidian architecture reached its zenith. The Brihadeshwara Temple at Tanjore and Nataraja Temple at Chidambaram are notable examples.
questions.solution_hi:
• गंगा घाटी तक अपने सफल उत्तरी अभियान के बाद, राजेंद्र प्रथम ने "गंगईकोंडचोल" (गंगा जीतने वाला चोल) की उपाधि धारण की।

• चोल वंश (985-1044 ईस्वी) के महत्वपूर्ण शासक।

• स्थापना: विजयालय द्वारा, जो पल्लवों के सामंत थे।

questions.q_en: Which of the following best describes the Chola system of local self-government?
options_en: Village assemblies (Ur and Sabha) exercised considerable autonomy in local matters.
Control by military garrisons stationed in the region.
Governance through a council of noble elites appointed by the king.
questions.solution_en:
• The Cholas were known for their highly decentralized local administration, where village assemblies (Ur for general population and Sabha for Brahmins) had significant authority in governance, especially concerning revenue and legal matters.

Further Insight:

• Important ruler of the Chola dynasty (985-1044 CE)

• Founding: By Vijayalaya, a feudatory of Pallavas. The Imperial Cholas were based in Tanjore.

• Key Rulers

○ Rajaraja I (985-1014 AD):

■ Expanded Chola empire, conquered Maldives, and built the Rajarajeshwara or Brihadeshwara temple at Thanjavur.

○ Rajendra I (1014-1044 AD):

■ Conquered Sri Lanka, assumed the title "Gangaikondachola," and built a new capital city, Gangaikondacholapuram.

○ Chola Architecture: Dravidian architecture reached its zenith. The Brihadeshwara Temple at Tanjore and Nataraja Temple at Chidambaram are notable examples
questions.solution_hi:
• चोल स्थानीय सरकार हेतु अत्यधिक विकेंद्रीकृत प्रशासन के लिए जाने जाते थे, जहाँ ग्राम सभाओं (सामान्य जनसंख्या हेतु उर व ब्राह्मणों हेतु सभा) को शासन में, विशेषकर राजस्व व कानूनी मामलों में, महत्वपूर्ण अधिकार प्राप्त था।

• चोल वंश (985-1044) के महत्वपूर्ण शासक।

questions.q_en: Which of the following monuments was built under the patronage of Rajaraja Chola I?
questions.solution_en:
• Rajaraja Chola I is credited with constructing the Brihadeshwara Temple at Thanjavur, one of the grandest achievements of Dravidian temple architecture.

• Meenakshi Temple in Madurai was associated with later Pandya rulers.

• Virupaksha Temple was built by the Chalukyas.

• Shore Temple was constructed by the Pallavas.

Further Insight:

• Brihadeshwara Temple (Thanjavur):

○ Built by Rajaraja Chola I.

○ UNESCO World Heritage Site.

○ Known for its massive dome and exquisite sculptures.

• Gangaikondacholisvaram Temple:

○ Constructed by Rajendra Chola I.

○ UNESCO World Heritage Site.

• Nataraja Temple (Chidambaram):

○ Dedicated to Lord Shiva in his dancing form.

○ Important pilgrimage site; known for its unique architecture and cultural significance.

• Airavatesvara Temple (Darasuram):

○ Built by Rajendra Chola II.

○ UNESCO World Heritage Site.
questions.solution_hi:
• राजराज चोल प्रथम को तंजावुर में बृहदीश्वर मंदिर बनवाने का श्रेय जाता है, जो द्रविड़ मंदिर स्थापत्य कला की सबसे भव्य उपलब्धियों में से एक है।

• मदुरै में मीनाक्षी मंदिर बाद के पांड्य शासकों से जुड़ा था।

• विरुपाक्ष मंदिर चालुक्यों द्वारा बनाया गया था।

questions.q_en: Who succeeded Harshavardhana as the ruler of the Vardhan dynasty after his death?
questions.solution_en:
• Harshavardhana died without a direct heir, and no significant ruler succeeded him, leading to the decline of the Vardhan dynasty.

• Rajyavardhana was Harshavardhana's elder brother but was killed by Sasanka before Harsha came to power.

• Grahavarman was Harsha's brother-in-law, married to his sister, and not his successor.

• Prabhakaravardhana was Harsha's father and had died earlier.

Further Insight:

• Vardhan Dynasty

○ Period: 6th - 7th century CE.

○ Capital: Thanesar.

○ Key Rulers:

■ Prabhakaravardhana: Expanded territory; father of Harshavardhana.

■ Rajyavardhana: Notable for defeating foreign invasions; killed by Sasanka of Bengal.

■ Harshavardhana:

• Unified northern India

• promoted Buddhism

• Hosted the Prayag Assembly

• authored "Nagananda."
questions.solution_hi:
• हर्षवर्धन बिना प्रत्यक्ष उत्तराधिकारी के निधन हुआ, व कोई महत्वपूर्ण शासक उनके उत्तराधिकारी नहीं बने, जिससे वर्धन वंश का पतन हुआ।

• राज्यवर्धन हर्षवर्धन के बड़े भाई थे परंतु हर्ष के सत्ता में आने से पहले शशांक द्वारा मारे गए।

• ग्रहवर्मन हर्ष के बहनोई थे।

questions.q_en: Which of the following literary works is attributed to a Rashtrakuta ruler?
questions.solution_en:
• Amoghavarsha I of the Rashtrakutas authored Kavirajamarga, an important work in Kannada literature, demonstrating his patronage of arts and culture.

• Arthashastra was authored by Kautilya (Chanakya).

• Shishupala Vadha was written by Magha, a poet in the Gupta era.

• Abhijnanasakuntalam was written by Kalidasa during the Gupta period.

Further Insight:

• Important Rulers of Rashtrakutas of Deccan (752-973)

○ Dantidurga (753-756):

■ Founded Rashtrakuta kingdom.

○ Krishna I (756-774):

■ Defeated Pallavas and built the famous Kailasanath (Shiva) temple at Ellora.

○ Amoghavarsha I (814-878):

■ Compared to Ashoka, built a new capital at Manyakheta. Authored Kavirajamarga (Kannada) and Prashnottara Ratnamalika (Sanskrit).
questions.solution_hi:
• राष्ट्रकूटों के अमोघवर्ष प्रथम ने कविराजमार्ग रचा, जो कन्नड़ साहित्य में एक महत्वपूर्ण कृति है, जो कला व संस्कृति के प्रति उनके संरक्षण को दर्शाती है।

• अर्थशास्त्र कौटिल्य (चाणक्य) द्वारा रचा गया था।

• शिशुपाल वध माघ द्वारा लिखा गया, गुप्त युग के एक कवि।

questions.q_en: Which Chola king is known for organizing a naval expedition to Southeast Asia?
questions.solution_en:
• Rajendra I is famous for sending a naval expedition to Southeast Asia, specifically against the Srivijaya kingdom, which expanded the Chola influence across the Bay of Bengal.

• Rajaraja I expanded Chola influence, but his campaigns were mainly focused on southern India and Sri Lanka.

• Vijayalaya Chola is the founder of the Chola dynasty but not known for naval expeditions.

• Kulottunga I had campaigns in Sri Lanka but didn't lead major naval expeditions to Southeast Asia.

Further Insight:

• Important ruler of the Chola dynasty (985-1044 CE)

• Founding: By Vijayalaya, a feudatory of Pallavas. The Imperial Cholas were based in Tanjore.

• Key Rulers

○ Rajaraja I (985-1014 AD):

■ Expanded Chola empire, conquered Maldives, and built the Rajarajeshwara or Brihadeshwara temple at Thanjavur.

○ Rajendra I (1014-1044 AD):

■ Conquered Sri Lanka, assumed the title "Gangaikondachola," and built a new capital city, Gangaikondacholapuram.

○ Chola Architecture: Dravidian architecture reached its zenith. The Brihadeshwara Temple at Tanjore and Nataraja Temple at Chidambaram are notable examples
questions.solution_hi:
• राजेंद्र प्रथम दक्षिण-पूर्व एशिया में एक नौसैनिक अभियान भेजने के लिए प्रसिद्ध हैं, विशेष रूप से श्रीविजय साम्राज्य के विरुद्ध, जिसने बंगाल की खाड़ी में चोल प्रभाव का विस्तार किया।

• राजराज प्रथम ने चोल प्रभाव का विस्तार किया, परंतु उनके अभियान मुख्यतः दक्षिण भारत व श्रीलंका पर केंद्रित थे।

questions.q_en:
Consider the following statements regarding Pulakeshin II:

a. Pulakeshin II expanded the Chalukya kingdom into northern India.

b. He defeated Harshavardhana and established the Narmada River as a key boundary.

c. He is credited with the construction of the Brihadeshwara Temple at Thanjavur.

Which of the above statements are correct?
questions.solution_en:
• Pulakeshin II famously defeated Harshavardhana and established the Narmada as a territorial boundary.

• Pulakeshin II did expand southward but primarily focused on consolidating power in the Deccan rather than northern India.

• The Brihadeshwara Temple was built by Rajaraja Chola I, not Pulakeshin II.

Further Insight:

• Chalukya Dynasty

○ Period: 6th - 8th century CE.

○ Key Ruler:

■ Pulakeshin II: Expanded the kingdom; defeated Harshavardhana, establishing the Narmada as a key boundary.

○ Capital: Badami.

○ Contributions:

■ Renowned for rock-cut and structural temples (e.g., Badami cave temples).

■ Patronage of Hinduism and Jainism, fostering regional art and architecture.
questions.solution_hi:
• पुलकेशिन द्वितीय ने प्रसिद्ध रूप से हर्षवर्धन को हराया व नर्मदा को क्षेत्रीय सीमा के रूप में स्थापित किया।

• पुलकेशिन द्वितीय ने दक्षिण की ओर विस्तार किया परंतु मुख्यतः उत्तर भारत के बजाय दक्कन में सत्ता सुदृढ़ करने पर केंद्रित रहे।

• बृहदीश्वर मंदिर राजराज चोल प्रथम द्वारा बनाया गया था, पुलकेशिन द्वितीय द्वारा नहीं।

questions.q_en: Which of the following Rajput clans was primarily responsible for defending India against Mahmud of Ghazni's invasions?
questions.solution_en:
• The Pratiharas were instrumental in defending western India against Mahmud of Ghazni's invasions, particularly during the reign of Nagabhata II.

• Chauhans resisted later Islamic invasions but not specifically Mahmud of Ghazni.

• The Guhilots were active in Mewar but didn't play a key role against Mahmud of Ghazni.

• Paramaras were known for their internal conflicts but didn't focus on Ghazni's invasions.

Further Insight:

• Chahamanas (Chauhans) (6th - 12th century)

○ Key Ruler: Prithviraj Chauhan

○ Region: Rajasthan and surrounding areas

○ The Chauhans were feudal lords under the Pratiharas and played a significant role in resisting Arab invasions and later establishing their independent rule in northern India.

• Paramaras of Malwa (9th - 14th century)

○ Region: Malwa (Central India)

○ They were initially vassals of the Rashtrakutas, but eventually, they became an independent force, known for their contributions to art, literature, and architecture.

• Chandellas of Bundelkhand (9th - 13th century)

○ Region: Bundelkhand (Central India)

○ They are best known for building the famous temples of Khajuraho, a UNESCO World Heritage site, and played a key role in central Indian politics.
questions.solution_hi:
• प्रतिहार महमूद गजनवी के आक्रमणों के विरुद्ध पश्चिमी भारत की रक्षा में महत्वपूर्ण थे, विशेषकर नागभट्ट द्वितीय के शासनकाल के दौरान।

• चौहानों ने बाद के इस्लामी आक्रमणों का प्रतिरोध किया परंतु विशेष रूप से महमूद गजनवी का नहीं।

• गुहिलोत मेवाड़ में सक्रिय थे।

questions.q_en:
Consider the following statements regarding the Tripartite Struggle for Kannauj:

a. The struggle was primarily between the Gurjara-Pratiharas, Palas, and Cholas.

b. Kannauj's significance lay in its strategic position on the Ganga trade route.

c. The Tripartite Struggle ultimately weakened all three participating dynasties.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.solution_en:
• The struggle was between the Gurjara-Pratiharas, Palas, and Rashtrakutas, not the Cholas.

• Kannauj's location made it commercially significant.

• The prolonged conflict weakened all three dynasties involved.

Further Insight:

• Tripartite Struggle for Kannauj Supremacy (750-1000 CE)

○ Major Empires: Gurjara-Pratihara (Western India), Palas (Eastern India), Rashtrakutas (Deccan).

○ Cause: Control over Kannauj, a commercially strategic location on the Ganga trade route and previously the capital of Harshavardhan.
questions.solution_hi:
• संघर्ष गुर्जर-प्रतिहार, पाल व राष्ट्रकूट के बीच था, चोलों के बीच नहीं।

• कन्नौज की स्थिति ने इसे वाणिज्यिक रूप से महत्वपूर्ण बनाया।

• लंबे संघर्ष ने तीनों शामिल वंशों को कमजोर किया।

• कन्नौज वर्चस्व हेतु त्रिपक्षीय संघर्ष (750-1000 ईस्वी)।

questions.q_en:
Consider the following statements about the Gurjara-Pratiharas:

a. The Pratiharas are credited with stopping Arab invasions east of the Indus River.

b. Nagabhata II rebuilt the Somnath Temple after its destruction by Mahmud of Ghazni.

c. Bhoja I, also known as Mihir Bhoja, was the most prominent ruler of the dynasty.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.solution_en:
• Pratiharas were responsible for stopping Arab invasions east of the Indus.

• Nagabhata II rebuilt the Somnath Temple after an earlier Arab raid, not after its destruction by Mahmud of Ghazni.

• Bhoja I, also called Mihir Bhoja, was the greatest ruler of the dynasty.

Further Insight:

• Important Rulers of Gurjara-Pratihara Dynasty (730-1036)

○ Nagabhatta I (730-760):

■ Famed for containing Arab invasions.

■ Defeated by Rashtrakuta king Dhruva.

○ Vatsaraja (780-800):

■ Made Kannauj his capital, initiating the "Tripartite Struggle."

■ Defeated Pala ruler Dharmapala and Rashtrakuta king Dantidurga.

○ Nagabhata II (805-833):

■ Conquered Kannauj and rebuilt Somnath temple after Arab raids.

○ Bhoja I / Mihir Bhoja (836-885):

■ Greatest Pratihara ruler, adopted the title 'Adivaraha.'
questions.solution_hi:
• प्रतिहार सिंधु के पूर्व में अरब आक्रमणों को रोकने हेतु उत्तरदायी थे।

• नागभट्ट द्वितीय ने एक पूर्व अरब छापे के बाद सोमनाथ मंदिर का पुनर्निर्माण किया, महमूद गजनवी द्वारा इसके विनाश के बाद नहीं।

• भोज प्रथम, जिन्हें मिहिर भोज भी कहा जाता है, वंश के सबसे महान शासक थे।

questions.q_en:
Consider the following statements about the Pala Dynasty:

a. Gopala, the founder of the Pala dynasty, established his rule through democratic means.

b. The Palas were ardent followers of Theravada Buddhism.

c. Dharampala established Vikramshila University.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.solution_en:
• Gopala was elected by regional chieftains, which is a unique aspect of his rise to power.

• Palas were followers of Mahayana Buddhism, not Theravada.

• Dharampala is known for establishing Vikramshila University.

Further Insight:

• Important ruler of the Palas of Bengal (750-1150)

○ Gopala (750 CE):

■ Founder of Pala Dynasty

■ Founded Odantapuri monastery, the second-largest after Nalanda.

○ Dharampala (770-810):

■ Founded Vikramshila University and revived Nalanda University.

○ Devapala (810-850):

■ Expanded empire, known for victories over Hunas, Gurjaras, and Dravidas.
questions.solution_hi:
• गोपाल का क्षेत्रीय सरदारों द्वारा चुनाव हुआ, जो उनके सत्ता में उदय का एक अनूठा पहलू है।

• पाल महायान बौद्ध धर्म के अनुयायी थे, थेरवाद के नहीं।

• धर्मपाल विक्रमशिला विश्वविद्यालय की स्थापना के लिए जाने जाते हैं।

• बंगाल के पालों (750-1150) के महत्वपूर्ण शासक।

questions.q_en:
Consider the following statements about the Rashtrakutas:

a. Amoghavarsha I is credited with building the famous Kailasanath Temple at Ellora.

b. The Rashtrakutas had friendly relations with the Abbasid Caliphate.

c. Krishna I was the first Rashtrakuta ruler to defeat the Pallavas.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.solution_en:
• Krishna I, not Amoghavarsha I, built the famous Kailasanath Temple at Ellora.

• Rashtrakutas had diplomatic and trade relations with the Abbasid Caliphate.

• Krishna I was the first Rashtrakuta ruler to defeat the Pallavas.

Further Insight:

• Important Rulers of Rashtrakutas of Deccan (752-973)

○ Dantidurga (753-756):

■ Founded Rashtrakuta kingdom.

○ Krishna I (756-774):

■ Defeated Pallavas and built the famous Kailasanath (Shiva) temple at Ellora.

○ Amoghavarsha I (814-878):

■ Compared to Ashoka, built a new capital at Manyakheta. Authored Kavirajamarga (Kannada) and Prashnottara Ratnamalika (Sanskrit).
questions.solution_hi:
• अमोघवर्ष प्रथम नहीं बल्कि कृष्ण प्रथम ने एलोरा में प्रसिद्ध कैलासनाथ मंदिर बनवाया।

• राष्ट्रकूटों के अब्बासी खलीफा के साथ राजनयिक व व्यापारिक संबंध थे।

• कृष्ण प्रथम पल्लवों को हराने वाले पहले राष्ट्रकूट शासक थे।

questions.q_en:
Consider the following statements regarding the Chola dynasty:

a. Rajaraja I conquered parts of Sri Lanka during his reign.

b. Rajendra I built a new capital city, Gangaikondacholapuram, after his campaign to the Ganga.

c. The Cholas are primarily remembered for their contributions to North Indian temple architecture.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.solution_en:
• Rajaraja I conquered northern parts of Sri Lanka.

• Rajendra I built Gangaikondacholapuram after his successful Ganga expedition.

• Cholas are renowned for their contributions to South Indian, specifically Dravidian, temple architecture.

Further Insight:

• Important ruler of the Chola dynasty (985-1044 CE)

• Founding: By Vijayalaya, a feudatory of Pallavas. The Imperial Cholas were based in Tanjore.

• Key Rulers

○ Rajaraja I (985-1014 AD):

■ Expanded Chola empire, conquered Maldives, and built the Rajarajeshwara or Brihadeshwara temple at Thanjavur.

○ Rajendra I (1014-1044 AD):

■ Conquered Sri Lanka, assumed the title "Gangaikondachola," and built a new capital city, Gangaikondacholapuram.
questions.solution_hi:
• राजराज प्रथम ने अपने शासनकाल में श्रीलंका के हिस्सों को जीता।

• राजेंद्र प्रथम ने अपने सफल गंगा अभियान के बाद गंगईकोंडचोलपुरम बनवाया।

• चोल दक्षिण भारतीय, विशेष रूप से द्रविड़, मंदिर स्थापत्य कला में अपने योगदान के लिए प्रसिद्ध हैं।

questions.q_en:
Consider the following statements about the Rajput clans:

a. The Paramaras of Malwa were initially vassals of the Rashtrakutas.

b. The Chandellas of Bundelkhand are best known for constructing the Khajuraho temples.

c. The Chauhans defeated the Ghurids in the Second Battle of Tarain.

Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.solution_en:
• Paramaras of Malwa initially served as vassals of the Rashtrakutas.

• Chandellas constructed the Khajuraho temples.

• Ghurids, led by Muhammad of Ghor, defeated the Chauhans in the Second Battle of Tarain (1192 CE).

Further Insight:

• Chahamanas (Chauhans) (6th - 12th century)

○ Key Ruler: Prithviraj Chauhan

○ Region: Rajasthan and surrounding areas

○ The Chauhans were feudal lords under the Pratiharas and played a significant role in resisting Arab invasions and later establishing their independent rule in northern India.

• Paramaras of Malwa (9th - 14th century)

○ Region: Malwa (Central India)

○ They were initially vassals of the Rashtrakutas, but eventually, they became an independent force, known for their contributions to art, literature, and architecture.

• Chandellas of Bundelkhand (9th - 13th century)

○ Region: Bundelkhand (Central India)

○ They are best known for building the famous temples of Khajuraho, a UNESCO World Heritage site, and played a key role in central Indian politics.
questions.solution_hi:
• मालवा के परमार शुरुआत में राष्ट्रकूटों के सामंत के रूप में सेवा करते थे।

• चंदेलों ने खजुराहो मंदिर बनवाए।

• मुहम्मद घोरी के नेतृत्व वाले घुरिदों ने द्वितीय तराइन युद्ध (1192 ईस्वी) में चौहानों को हराया।

• चाहमान (चौहान) (छठी-बारहवीं शताब्दी)।

questions.q_en:
Consider the following statements regarding the Vardhan Dynasty:

a. Harshavardhana initially ruled over both Kannauj and Thanesar.

b. Rajyavardhana was killed by the ruler of Bengal, Sasanka.

c. Harshavardhana was a follower of Mahayana Buddhism, and he organized the famous Prayag Assembly.

d. Harshavardhana authored the play "Nagananda" in Sanskrit.

Which of the above statements are correct?
questions.solution_en:
• Harshavardhana ruled over both Kannauj and Thanesar after the death of his brother Rajyavardhana.

• Rajyavardhana was indeed killed by Sasanka, the ruler of Bengal.

• Harshavardhana followed Mahayana Buddhism and organized the Prayag Assembly to distribute wealth.

• Harshavardhana is credited with writing "Nagananda" in Sanskrit.

Further Insight:

• Vardhan Dynasty or Pushyabhuti Dynasty

○ Period: 6th - 7th century CE.

○ Capital: Thanesar.

○ Key Rulers:

■ Prabhakaravardhana: Expanded territory; father of Harshavardhana.

■ Rajyavardhana: Notable for defeating foreign invasions; killed by Sasanka of Bengal.

■ Harshavardhana:

• Unified northern India

• promoted Buddhism

• Hosted the Prayag Assembly

• authored "Nagananda."
questions.solution_hi:
• हर्षवर्धन ने अपने भाई राज्यवर्धन की मृत्यु के बाद कन्नौज व थानेसर दोनों पर शासन किया।

• राज्यवर्धन वास्तव में बंगाल के शासक शशांक द्वारा मारे गए।

• हर्षवर्धन ने महायान बौद्ध धर्म का पालन किया व धन वितरित करने हेतु प्रयाग सभा आयोजित की।

questions.q_en: The Famous Badami caves built by which of the following dynasty?
questions.solution_en:
The Famous Badami Caves were built by the Chalukya dynasty. These rock-cut caves, located in Karnataka, date back to the 6th century and are known for their stunning architecture and intricate sculptures.

Further Insight:

• Chalukya Dynasty

○ Period: 6th - 8th century CE.

○ Key Ruler:

■ Pulakeshin II: Expanded the kingdom; defeated Harshavardhana, establishing the Narmada as a key boundary.

○ Capital: Badami.

○ Contributions:

■ Renowned for rock-cut and structural temples (e.g., Badami cave temples).

■ Patronage of Hinduism and Jainism, fostering regional art and architecture.
questions.solution_hi:
प्रसिद्ध बादामी गुफाएँ चालुक्य वंश द्वारा बनाई गई थीं। कर्नाटक में स्थित ये शैल-कट गुफाएँ छठी शताब्दी की हैं व अपनी अद्भुत स्थापत्य कला व जटिल मूर्तियों के लिए जानी जाती हैं।

• चालुक्य वंश

○ अवधि: छठी-आठवीं शताब्दी ईस्वी।
